# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b86 — Announce real physical device errors

Beta86 adds fault monitoring for the existing Home Assistant error information reported by physical devices controlled or monitored by HEM. **No additional error/fault sensor is created.** Each controlled device receives one configurable HEM **Announce device errors** switch, ON by default, and the HEM dashboard displays the original HA error with a link to that native entity.

## Native error sources, not synthetic diagnostics

- Read explicit manufacturer error attributes on the original physical source entity (e.g. `error_code`, `fault_code`, `error_message`, `error_description`, `error_info`, `fault_detail`) and existing registered `sensor.*_error`, `sensor.*_fault` or `binary_sensor.*_problem` entities.
- Associate related errors **only through the exact underlying HA Device Registry ID**, never by similar device names or another device in the same area. Disabled, unrelated or HEM-generated entities cannot become new fault sources.
- Represent active native error code, severity, description, source entity ID and the bounded manufacturer diagnostic details on the managed-device card. Tap the source to open the **original Home Assistant error entity**. A temporary `unknown`/`unavailable` report is not a confirmed error or recovery; the last known fault remains visible as historical/uncertain information.
- Do not interpret `error_code: 0`, an OFF problem binary sensor, or stale `last error` metadata as a new active fault. Error counters or unrelated numeric sensors do not create false alarms.

## One default-ON switch for each controlled device

Each logical managed controller receives a **switch** for its own error announcements (`announce_device_errors`), with a default of **ON**, including previously configured devices. The switch remains editable when physical equipment is temporarily unavailable. Changing it writes only the HEM option and never sends a power, HVAC, PID, relay or reset command.

## Announcements include the complete relevant error information

When an error first appears, changes its code/description or escalates in severity, HEM sends a device-specific message containing **device name, room, original source entity ID, exact error code, severity, description and any manufacturer-provided error details** (for example an affected part or suggested action). Error details are passed in the **actual message text to Announcement Hub**; they are not lost or replaced by a generic "device error" notice.

- If the configured Announcement Hub is running, HEM submits one warning-level job with `use_ai: false`, so AI cannot invent or rewrite diagnostic codes. Hub alone owns occupied-room routing, mobile/TTS delivery, retries, sleep/quiet policies and fallback. A running Hub's unacknowledged job must **not** trigger duplicate HEM delivery.
- Otherwise HEM uses the configured per-room native Home Assistant notification recipients, eligible TTS when enabled, and a single built-in persistent HA notification as the final visual fallback.
- Only a newly reported error or changed error signature can produce another announcement. HA startup, repeated identical states, unrelated attribute refreshes and unknown/unavailable diagnostics do not replay the same fault. A manufacturer-confirmed clear allows a later recurrence of the same error to notify again.
- Multiple HEM channels belonging to the same physical HA device do not produce duplicate physical error announcements.

## Safety and compatibility

**Read-only device fault monitoring:** no hardware actuation, reset, power cycle, increased PID demand or changed controller permission. The existing safety repairs from Beta83–85 remain intact: no powered-device relay cutoff, minimum verified-idle cooldown, native command Resume reconciliation, PID approval controls and room/sleep/window protections. The implementation preserves the canonical `environment_manager` domain, existing physical source entities, device identifiers, areas and all stored settings.

## Validation

The Beta86 validation and release checks cover native HA device-registry association, unrelated same-room and disabled entities, fresh manufacturer code/message/detail extraction, transmission of detailed error attributes all the way to the **Announcement Hub payload**, default-ON and per-device switch independence, deduplication and unavailable-state handling, actual Chromium card navigation and toggling, translation catalogs, and the existing device, PID, relay, sleep, window, and Resume regressions. Tests exercise simulated HA services only; live hardware and companion notification delivery require post-install observation.

## Installation

Update the existing Home Environment Manager via **HACS to v0.6.0b86**, then restart Home Assistant and refresh the HEM dashboard. On each controlled physical device, you will see **Announce errors** enabled by default. If its native HA integration reports a real active error, HEM will show that exact error on the card and announce the code and available error information. If the HA integration does not expose any error status or diagnostic entity, HEM cannot invent one.
